summary: abandoned session still holds the data key in server RAM until TTL (held=True) — but the operator ceiling is now 300s (2026-09-16 fix), exactly matching the consent copy's 'held in memory for up to 5 minutes'; residual exposure is the disclosed 5-minute window, not an hour
stolen session token unusable by another account: 403 processing_session_invalid (thief still needs the victim bearer token too)

post-run GC scan of 20000 tracked container(s) for the plaintext marker: 0 lingering copy-location(s)  (CPython refcounting frees this path promptly; the enclave docstring's honest caveat covers exception paths/analyzer-held refs, not this one)
derive_master_key refuses iterations < 100000 on both platforms and the floor is pinned at the 100k/600k contract (MIN_ITERATIONS=100000, KDF_ITERATIONS=600000)

a hand-rolled 1-iteration derivation still registers (201) — the server never sees the password, so client work factors are structurally unverifiable; the floor removes every accidental/honest downgrade path

production encrypt() signature is ['key', 'plaintext', 'aad'] — no nonce parameter; two identical calls always differ (fresh=True); fixed-nonce output is only reachable via the unmistakably-named encrypt_with_nonce, mirrored in the mobile envelope.ts
random 96-bit nonces, 10000 entries under one key: P(collision) ≈ 6.31e-22 — negligible within the per-user quota; risk is structural only if the quota is raised or the seam above is used

password change PUT /account/password=True, corpus rekey POST /processing/rekey=True, login-credential rotation PUT /account/credential=True: a compromised master secret now has an in-band recovery and a v2 password change no longer costs O(corpus) re-encryption. Both key-swapping endpoints require a possession probe — a live owner-bound X-Processing-Token session whose popped key must AUTHENTICATE stored ciphertext (wrong key: 403 envelope_key_mismatch; guards found in endpoint source: True) — so a stolen bearer alone cannot lock the real user out

16 edge-case AAD vectors written to redteam/results/corpus/aad_corpus.json (committed redteam/aad_corpus.json stays the read-only fixture the TS side replays); verdict comes from the TS-side comparison (mobile redteam spec)
